def-fixed-design-linear-regression-model:
## Definition

Let $n,p\ge1$ be integers and let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ be a fixed matrix.
A **fixed-design first-moment linear regression model** is a parametric
statistical experiment on $(\mathbb R^n,\mathcal B(\mathbb R^n))$ with parameter
set $\mathbb R^p$, laws $(P_\beta)_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}$, and observed vector
$Y(y)=y$, such that every coordinate of $Y$ is integrable under $P_\beta$ and
$$
\mathbb E_\beta Y=X\beta\qquad(\beta\in\mathbb R^p).
$$
Here $\mathcal B(\mathbb R^n)$ is the Borel sigma-algebra, and expectation is
taken under the particular law $P_\beta$. The residual vector
$\epsilon_\beta:=Y-X\beta$ therefore has coordinatewise mean zero. The phrase
**fixed design** means that $X$ is held constant in this experiment; it carries
no probability law or assignment mechanism for $X$.

This definition states only the first-moment model. It imposes no covariance,
independence, or Gaussian assumption. Such assumptions must be stated where
used.
lem-linear-contrast-statistics-are-borel:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$ and $a\in\mathbb R^n$. The linear map
$$
\ell_a:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R,\qquad \ell_a(y)=a^Ty,
$$
is measurable from the Euclidean Borel space $\mathbb R^n$ to the Borel space
$\mathbb R$.
def-least-squares-solution-set:
## Definition

For integers $n,p\ge1$, a matrix $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$, and a response
vector $y\in\mathbb R^n$, define the **least-squares solution set**
$$
\mathcal B_{\mathrm{LS}}(y):=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{b\in\mathbb R^p}\|y-Xb\|_2^2.
$$
This is a set-valued definition; it does not select one coefficient vector.
The next theorem proves that the set is nonempty and identifies the fitted
vector and residual as unique, including when $X$ is rank-deficient.
thm-least-squares-fitted-vector-and-solu:
## Statement

Let $n,p\ge1$, $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$, $y\in\mathbb R^n$, and
$C=\operatorname{col}(X)\subseteq\mathbb R^n$. For the least-squares solution
set $\mathcal B_{\mathrm{LS}}(y)$ of
[[def-least-squares-solution-set]], the following hold:

1. $\mathcal B_{\mathrm{LS}}(y)$ is nonempty, and $b$ is in it exactly when
   $X^T(Xb-y)=0$.
2. If $b_0\in\mathcal B_{\mathrm{LS}}(y)$, then
   $\mathcal B_{\mathrm{LS}}(y)=b_0+\ker X$.
3. Every least-squares solution has the same fitted vector $P_Cy$ and residual
   $y-P_Cy$.
4. The affine solution set has dimension $p-\operatorname{rank}(X)$.

The theorem makes no statistical moment or distributional assumption.
def-linear-estimability-in-fixed-design:
## Definition

In a fixed-design first-moment regression model with parameter
$\beta\in\mathbb R^p$, a **linear contrast** is the estimand
$$
\psi_c(\beta):=c^T\beta,\qquad c\in\mathbb R^p.
$$
The contrast is **linearly estimable** if there is a fixed vector
$a\in\mathbb R^n$ such that the statistic $a^TY$ is unbiased for $\psi_c$ at
every parameter value:
$$
\mathbb E_\beta[a^TY]=c^T\beta\qquad\text{for every }\beta\in\mathbb R^p.
$$
The vector $a$ may depend on the fixed design and on $c$, but not on the
observed response or on the unknown parameter. The map $y\mapsto a^Ty$ is a
measurable statistic by
[[lem-linear-contrast-statistics-are-borel-measurable]] and
[[def-statistic-and-estimator]].
thm-linear-estimability-iff-row-space:
## Statement

In a fixed-design first-moment regression model with $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$,
a contrast $c^T\beta$ is linearly estimable if and only if
$$
c\in\operatorname{row}(X)=\operatorname{im}(X^T),
$$
equivalently if and only if there exists $a\in\mathbb R^n$ with $X^Ta=c$.
Whenever this holds, $a^TY$ is unbiased for $c^T\beta$ for every $\beta$.
Here $\operatorname{row}(X)$ is defined as the image of the transpose map.
thm-ols-unbiasedness-and-covariance-full:
## Statement

Let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ have full column rank in a fixed-design
first-moment regression model. Suppose for some $\sigma^2>0$ the error vector
$\epsilon_\beta:=Y-X\beta$ has finite second moments,
$\mathbb E_\beta\epsilon_\beta=0$, and
$\operatorname{Cov}_\beta(\epsilon_\beta)=\sigma^2 I_n$ for every $\beta$,
where the vector covariance matrix has entries
$\operatorname{Cov}_\beta(\epsilon_{\beta,i},\epsilon_{\beta,j})$.
Then the unique least-squares estimator is
$$
\widehat\beta=(X^TX)^{-1}X^TY,
$$
it is unbiased for $\beta$, and its covariance matrix is
$$
\operatorname{Cov}_\beta(\widehat\beta)=\sigma^2(X^TX)^{-1}.
$$
No Gaussian assumption is made.
thm-gauss-markov-for-fixed-design-regres:
## Statement

Let $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ have full column rank in a fixed-design
first-moment regression model. Suppose
$\operatorname{Cov}_\beta(\epsilon_\beta)=\sigma^2 I_n$ for a fixed
$\sigma^2>0$, where the vector covariance matrix has entries
$\operatorname{Cov}_\beta(\epsilon_{\beta,i},\epsilon_{\beta,j})$. For every
contrast $c^T\beta$, the OLS estimate
$c^T\widehat\beta$ is unbiased and has variance no larger than any other
linear unbiased estimator of that contrast. Thus OLS is **best linear
unbiased (BLUE)** for every estimable contrast. Here “best” means minimum
variance within the class of linear unbiased estimators; Gaussianity is not
assumed.
